Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

You are an adversarial verifier. A finder claims this is LEGACY code safe to delete. Try hard to REFUTE it.

Finding: repo=andesim path=tests/fixtures/rt_all_gprs.S lines=3-14, 58-139 kind=dead-code-block
Claim: Header describes the removed 'across QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2' flow and the entire phase_c GPR verify sweep (spill + 27 CHECK_BASE macros + spilled-reg checks, ~80 lines) sits after the exit marker where vsim never executes it, so the full-GPR-survival guard is silently dead.
Evidence given: vsim exits 200 at `slti x0,x0,0x5A1` (line 56); run_e2e.sh:90 passes no CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT; the harness only asserts exit codes (tests/e2e.sh:204,231); rt_csr_survival.S:12-16 records that post-exit-marker phase_c guards died when the QEMU2 handback was removed.

Repo roots: andesim=/home/nick/work/andesim, vsim=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim.
Checks you MUST do:
1. Read the file/lines yourself — does the claim match reality?
2. grep BOTH repos (tracked files) for references: filename, function names, symbols, script names, make targets, cmake targets, doc links.
3. Check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/*, Makefiles, CMake, and CLAUDE.md/docs for indirect usage (variable-built names, glob patterns like test_*.sh runners).
4. git log --follow -5 on the file: was it recently touched for a live feature?
5. Is it an INTENTIONAL fallback/compat layer per CLAUDE.md (e.g. semihost_exit.inc)?
If ANY live reference or intentional-keep reason exists, verdict isLegacy=false. Default to false when uncertain. If true, give the exact deleteScope.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",

"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.

Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.

Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. 1	// rt_all_gprs.S
2	//
3	// Tier-1 fixture: full sweep of x1..x31 across QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2.
4	// Each register survives the round-trip with its 64-bit value intact.
5	//
6	// Phase A (QEMU1):
7	//   x5 = 0x00002000 (also serves as Phase C spill base).
8	//   x_i = 0xA000_0000_0000_0000 + i for i in {1..4, 6..31}.
9	// Phase B (vsim):  no-op.
10	// Phase C (QEMU2):
11	//   Spill x6, x28, x29 (sacrificed below).
12	//   Verify x_i directly for i in {1..4, 7..27, 30..31, then 5}.
13	//   Verify spilled x6, x28, x29 against expected.
14	//   Exit code = first mismatching reg num, or 0 on full pass.
15	
16	#include "semihost_exit.inc"
17	
18	.section .text
19	.globl _start
20	_start:
21	    li      x6, 0xA000000000000000   // temp base for ADDI sweep
22	    addi    x1,  x6, 1
23	    addi    x2,  x6, 2

32	    addi    x13, x6, 13
33	    addi    x14, x6, 14
34	    addi    x15, x6, 15
35	    addi    x16, x6, 16
36	    addi    x17, x6, 17
37	    addi    x18, x6, 18
38	    addi    x19, x6, 19
39	    addi    x20, x6, 20

47	    addi    x28, x6, 28
48	    addi    x29, x6, 29
49	    addi    x30, x6, 30
50	    addi    x31, x6, 31
51	    addi    x6,  x6, 6               // x6 = 0xA000_..._6
52	    li      x5, 0x00002000           // x5 = spill base (also its expected value)
53	
54	    slti   x0, x0,  0x5A0                 // QEMU1 drains, exits
55

61	    sd      x28, 8(x5)

103	    // Verify x5 directly (still holds 0x00002000).
104	    bnez    x29, check_spilled
105	    li      x28, 0x00002000
106	    beq     x5, x28, check_spilled
107	    addi    x29, x0, 5
108	
109	check_spilled:

111	    bnez    x29, check_x28
112	    ld      x28, 0(x5)
113	    li      x6, 0xA000000000000000
114	    addi    x6, x6, 6

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
21	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
22	#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this
23	#                              privilege (L6: 0=U, 1=S, 3=M).
24	#   CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=<re>     assert the vsim leg's output (guest UART rides
25	#                              it) matches this grep -E pattern -- the hook
26	#                              for fixtures that verify a result INSIDE the
27	#                              ROI and print a verdict (code after the exit
28	#                              marker never runs on the vsim leg).
29	#   ILM_SIZE / DLM_SIZE  LM content transport override, in bytes. Unset =
30	#                        probe $VSIM_BIN --describe (mirrors the driver's
31	#                        wiring); 0 = force that memory's transport OFF
32	#                        (negative-control knob).
33	#   CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1  assert the vsim leg dumped its exit-time LM
34	#                        content next to its state file AND that it equals
35	#                        the entry-time content byte-for-byte (valid for a
36	#                        ROI that does not WRITE the TCM -- closes the
37	#                        transport loop through the real RTL SRAM).
38	#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.
39	#   QEMU_CPU        -cpu argument for both QEMU legs (default
40	#                   andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512, pairing the default vsim
41	#                   engine). Override together with VSIM_BIN to run a
42	#                   fixture on another engine, e.g. the S/U-capable
43	#                   ax66_makatau for the rt_priv_* fixtures (the default
44	#                   ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only).
45	
46	set -euo pipefail
47	
48	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
49	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
50	. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"
51	
52	FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
53	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
54	TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-marker}"
55	QEMU_CPU="${QEMU_CPU:-andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512}"
56	
57	hybrid_resolve_paths
58	
59	NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
60	NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"
61	
62	case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
63	  marker) ;;
64	  pc)
65	    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
66	      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
67	      exit 77
68	    fi
69	    # ROI_START / ROI_END name the two switch PCs (0x address or symbol in
70	    # $VSIM_ELF). ./andesim run always passes them explicitly. When a caller
71	    # leaves BOTH unset (e.g. the bulk runner scripts/run_e2e.sh), derive them
72	    # from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via objdump, so pc mode needs no
73	    # per-fixture config and no planted boundary symbols. A partial set or a
74	    # derivation miss falls through to roi_resolve_pair's required-vars error.
75	    if [ -z "${ROI_START:-}" ] && [ -z "${ROI_END:-}" ]; then
76	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}}"
77	      OBJDUMP="${OBJDUMP:-riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump}"
78	      if command -v "$OBJDUMP" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
79	         && MARKERS=$(roi_markers_from_disasm "$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$VSIM_ELF")"); then
80	        ROI_START="0x${MARKERS%% *}"
81	        ROI_END="0x${MARKERS##* }"
82	        export ROI_START ROI_END
83	      fi
84	    fi
85	    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
86	    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
87	    ;;
88	  *)
89	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use marker|pc)"
90	    exit 1
91	    ;;
92	esac
93	
94	# 128 MB program RAM matches the QEMU virt machine default. L26/F2: the
95	# physical mmap reserves one V-scratch page (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES =
96	# 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) ABOVE the program's RAM, so the V-transport
97	# scratch (vsim parks it at the mmap top page) sits past anything the program
98	# can address. Mirrors the andesim driver (shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes).
99	# Read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from the shared ABI so this tracks the header
100	# (the ceiling moved 64 -> 128 once already) instead of hardcoding it.
101	VLEN_BYTES_MAX=$(awk '/^#define HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX/ {print $3}' \
102	  "$SCRIPT_DIR/../include/hybrid/state_abi.h")
103	[ -n "$VLEN_BYTES_MAX" ] || { echo "e2e: cannot read HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX from state_abi.h" >&2; exit 1; }
104	PROGRAM_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
105	V_SCRATCH_BYTES=$((32 * VLEN_BYTES_MAX))
106	SHARED_SIZE=$((PROGRAM_SIZE + V_SCRATCH_BYTES))
107	SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
108	STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
109	STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
110	SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
111	# mktemp names carry no dots, so the .* globs match exactly the legs'
112	# sidecars (state.ilm/.dlm today, any future suffix for free).
113	trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_QEMU".* \
114	            "$STATE_VSIM" "$STATE_VSIM".* "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
115	truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"
116	
117	PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
118	VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
119	
120	# LM/HVM content transport (ROADMAP_ilm_dlm, ROADMAP_hvm): mirror the
121	# driver's run_plan wiring. The engine's --describe reports its memories in
122	# BYTES; when a size is > 0 the QEMU plugin drains that memory's content to
123	# a sidecar next to the state file and the vsim leg backdoor-loads it
124	# (--ilm/--dlm/--hvm). An engine without the memory (or an older binary
125	# whose --describe lacks the field) adds nothing. ILM_SIZE/DLM_SIZE/HVM_SIZE
126	# env override the probe; 0 forces that memory's transport off
127	# (negative-control knob).
128	#
129	# QEMU's memory GEOMETRY is synced separately and ALWAYS (lm_geom, from the
130	# engine's describe -- the raw analog of the driver's
131	# --print-qemu-config/-readconfig sync), so a transport-off negative still
132	# runs the guest against the engine's real geometry. This matters twice:
133	# QEMU's compiled-in ILM default is 2 MB at 0x0, which SHADOWS the program
134	# image at 0x100000 the moment a guest sets milmb.EN (the engine's real
135	# 64 KB ends at 0xFFFF); and QEMU's HVM default is 1 BYTE
136	# (hvm_size_pow_2=0), which would fault an HVM fixture's fill outright.
137	# Probe the engine's real sizes ONCE; lm_geom always uses these, while the
138	# *_SIZE transport knobs default to them but may be overridden (0 = the
139	# negative-control off switch).
140	ILM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int ilm_size)
141	DLM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int dlm_size)
142	HVM_REAL=$(hybrid_describe_int hvm_size)
143	ILM_SIZE="${ILM_SIZE:-$ILM_REAL}"
144	DLM_SIZE="${DLM_SIZE:-$DLM_REAL}"
145	HVM_SIZE="${HVM_SIZE:-$HVM_REAL}"
146	VSIM_LM_ARGS=()
147	QEMU_LM_ARGS=()
148	lm_geom() {  # $1 ilm|dlm|hvm, $2 engine bytes ("" or 0 = engine has none)
149	  [ -n "$2" ] && [ "$2" -gt 0 ] || return 0
150	  if [ "$1" = hvm ]; then
151	    # QEMU's HVM geometry property is a power of two, not bytes.
152	    local p=0 v=$2
153	    while [ "$v" -gt 1 ]; do v=$((v >> 1)); p=$((p + 1)); done
154	    QEMU_LM_ARGS+=(-global "driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=hvm_size_pow_2,value=$p")
155	  else
156	    QEMU_LM_ARGS+=(-global "driver=riscv.andes.ae350.soc,property=$1_size,value=$2")
157	  fi
158	}
159	lm_wire() {  # $1 ilm|dlm|hvm, $2 size in bytes ("" or 0 = transport off)
160	  [ -n "$2" ] && [ "$2" -gt 0 ] || return 0
161	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,$1_size=$2"
162	  VSIM_LM_ARGS+=("--$1" "$STATE_QEMU.$1")
163	}
164	lm_geom ilm "$ILM_REAL"
165	lm_geom dlm "$DLM_REAL"
166	lm_geom hvm "$HVM_REAL"
167	lm_wire ilm "$ILM_SIZE"
168	lm_wire dlm "$DLM_SIZE"
169	lm_wire hvm "$HVM_SIZE"
170	if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
171	  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
172	  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
173	fi
174	
175	# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
176	# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
177	# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
178	VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
179	if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
180	  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
181	  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
182	    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
183	  fi
184	fi
185	
186	echo "[$FIXTURE 1/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] QEMU 1: drain entry state"
187	# timeout: a guest that wedges pre-marker (e.g. a TCM overlay shadowing its
188	# own image) would otherwise hang this leg forever -- QEMU runs at MHz, so
189	# the vsim-leg budget is generous here.
190	set +e
191	timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_QEMU" \
192	  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
193	  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
194	  -cpu "$QEMU_CPU" \
195	  -nographic \
196	  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
197	  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
198	  "${QEMU_LM_ARGS[@]}" \
199	  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,$PLUGIN_ARGS" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
200	QEMU1_RC=$?
201	set -e
202	
203	if [ "$QEMU1_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
204	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
205	  exit 1
206	fi
207	
208	if [ ! -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
209	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: QEMU 1 did not produce state"
210	  exit 1
211	fi
212	
213	echo "[$FIXTURE 2/2 mode=$TRIGGER_MODE] vsim: resume + drain"
214	set +e
215	timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
216	  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
217	  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
218	  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
219	  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
220	  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
221	  "${VSIM_TRIG_ARGS[@]}" \
222	  "${VSIM_LM_ARGS[@]}" \
223	  "${VSIM_KANATA_ARGS[@]}" </dev/null >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
224	VSIM_RC=$?
225	set -e
226	
227	# vsim drained on the exit trigger and exited 200 (kExitHandoffToQemu).
228	# Anything else is a hard failure: the cycle figure is only valid when vsim
229	# drained cleanly.
230	if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
231	  echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim expected exit 200 (drain), got $VSIM_RC"
232	  echo "--- sim log ---"
233	  cat "$SIM_LOG"
234	  exit 1
235	fi
236	
237	# LM/HVM exit-dump check: vsim dumps its ILM/DLM/HVM content next to the
238	# handoff-out state file; for a ROI that never writes those memories, the
239	# exit bytes must equal the entry bytes -- one byte-exact loop through
240	# plugin drain -> sidecar -> backdoor load -> RTL SRAM -> exit dump.
241	if [ "${CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS:-0}" = "1" ]; then
242	  for pair in "ilm:${ILM_SIZE:-0}" "dlm:${DLM_SIZE:-0}" "hvm:${HVM_SIZE:-0}"; do
243	    kind="${pair%%:*}"; sz="${pair##*:}"
244	    [ -n "$sz" ] && [ "$sz" -gt 0 ] || continue
245	    if [ ! -f "$STATE_VSIM.$kind" ]; then
246	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim did not dump $STATE_VSIM.$kind at exit"
247	      exit 1
248	    fi
249	    if ! cmp -s "$STATE_QEMU.$kind" "$STATE_VSIM.$kind"; then
250	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: $kind exit content differs from entry content:"
251	      cmp "$STATE_QEMU.$kind" "$STATE_VSIM.$kind" | head -3
252	      exit 1
253	    fi
254	  done
255	  echo "[$FIXTURE lm-exit] PASS: exit LM/HVM content matches entry byte-for-byte"
256	fi
257	
258	# In-ROI verdict check: the guest printed its result on the vsim leg's UART.
259	if [ -n "${CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT:-}" ]; then
260	  if grep -qE "$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT" "$SIM_LOG"; then
261	    echo "[$FIXTURE vsim-stdout] PASS: matched '$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT'"
262	  else
263	    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: vsim output did not match '$CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT'"
264	    echo "--- sim log (tail) ---"
265	    tail -25 "$SIM_LOG"
266	    exit 1
267	  fi
268	fi
269	
270	# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
271	# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
272	# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
273	# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
274	# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
275	read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }
276	if [ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] && [ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]; then
277	  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
278	  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
279	  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
280	  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
281	  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
282	  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
283	  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
284	    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
285	    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
286	    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
287	    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
288	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
289	      exit 1
290	    fi
291	  fi
292	  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
293	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
294	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
295	    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
296	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
297	      exit 1
298	    fi
299	    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
300	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
301	      exit 1
302	    fi
303	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
304	  fi
305	fi
306	
307	echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"
308

require VSIM_QEMU   "$VSIM_QEMU"
require VSIM_PLUGIN "$VSIM_PLUGIN"
require VSIM_BIN    "$VSIM_BIN"

export VSIM_QEMU VSIM_PLUGIN VSIM_BIN

REQUIRED_ELFS=(
  handoff_roundtrip rt_pc_jump rt_sign_bits rt_abi_aliases rt_long_roi
  rt_all_gprs rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh rt_csr_survival rt_shared_mem
  rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode
  rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_fcsr rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs
  rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill
)
need_build=0
for f in "${REQUIRED_ELFS[@]}"; do
  [[ -e "$TEST_DIR/$f.elf" ]] || need_build=1
done
if (( need_build )); then
  step "building test ELFs in $TEST_DIR"
  make -C "$TEST_DIR" -j
fi

# Round-trip fixtures: name|fixture-env-prefix. All run on the unified
# e2e.sh harness (shared /dev/shm mmap). The TRIGGER_MODE env is
# injected per iteration based on $MODE. Negative drivers live in
# NEG_TESTS and run once regardless of mode.
RT_TESTS=(
  "handoff_roundtrip|FIXTURE=handoff_roundtrip"
  "rt_pc_jump|FIXTURE=rt_pc_jump"
  "rt_sign_bits|FIXTURE=rt_sign_bits"
  "rt_abi_aliases|FIXTURE=rt_abi_aliases"
  "rt_long_roi|FIXTURE=rt_long_roi"
  "rt_all_gprs|FIXTURE=rt_all_gprs"
  "rt_mem_loadstore|FIXTURE=rt_mem_loadstore"
  "rt_unaligned_lh|FIXTURE=rt_unaligned_lh"
  "rt_csr_survival|FIXTURE=rt_csr_survival"
  "rt_m_ext_counters|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_counters"
  "rt_m_ext_trigcause|FIXTURE=rt_m_ext_trigcause"
  "rt_shared_mem|FIXTURE=rt_shared_mem"
  "rt_c_hello|FIXTURE=rt_c_hello"
  "rt_c_printf|FIXTURE=rt_c_printf"
  "rt_c_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_fcsr|FIXTURE=rt_c_fcsr"
  "rt_c_v_regs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_regs"
  "rt_c_v_csrs|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_csrs"
  "rt_c_v_matmul|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_matmul TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_v_fill|FIXTURE=rt_c_v_fill"
  "rt_c_static_buf|FIXTURE=rt_c_static_buf"
  "rt_c_dlm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_dlm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=DLM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
  "rt_c_ilm_code|FIXTURE=rt_c_ilm_code CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=ILM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1"
  "rt_c_hvm_data|FIXTURE=rt_c_hvm_data CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=HVM_OK CHECK_LM_EXIT_SIDECARS=1 TIMEOUT=120"
)

NEG_TESTS=(
  "rt_corrupt_state|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_corrupt_state.sh"
  "rt_lm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_lm_transport_off.sh"
  "rt_hvm_transport_off|bash $HARNESS/drivers/rt_hvm_transport_off.sh"
)

# Heavyweight round-trip fixtures, run SEQUENTIALLY after the parallel
# pool drains. The L6 privilege fixtures need an S/U-capable engine pair
# (the default ax45mpv_premium RTL is M-mode-only,
# NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1), and the only built RV64 one is
# ax66_makatau -- whose Verilator binary runs 32 threads. Two of those in
# the parallel pool saturate the box and time out BOTH themselves and the
# lighter default-engine tests, so they get the machine to themselves.
# Same entry format as RT_TESTS; both trigger modes still apply.
SERIAL_RT_TESTS=(
  "rt_priv_smode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_smode CHECK_PRIV=1 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
  "rt_priv_umode|FIXTURE=rt_priv_umode CHECK_PRIV=0 TIMEOUT=300 VSIM_BIN=$VSIM_BUILD/sim_ax66_makatau QEMU_CPU=andes-ax66,vlen=128"
)

MODE="${MODE:-both}"
case "$MODE" in
  marker|pc|both) ;;
  *) fail "MODE must be one of marker|pc|both (got: $MODE)"; exit 1 ;;
esac

default_jobs() {
  local n=1 shm_free shm_cap
  n=$(nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)
  if [[ -d /dev/shm ]]; then
    shm_free=$(df -m --output=avail /dev/shm 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | tr -d ' ')
